The home networks are the ones under Home network; they can be named there without switching the sign-in without a password on.
sections.path: System > Apps > At home, On the road

sections.title: Every number, the way you want it
sections.body: Every card with a measured number can be a dial, LED bars across or upright, seven-segment digits or a chart. Full at and Empty at set the span, Yellow from and Red from the colours; red below yellow means low numbers are the bad ones. A chart shows the last hour, six hours or a day.

small: A chart of a day showed only its second half; it now fetches the hours it shows.
Thanks to bluedsticker for the app catalog (#37) and to naamah75 for the drawings (#39).

0.41.1.lead: The bar stays clear of the iPad blur on every page now, from signing in to the settings.

sections.title: One bar for every page
sections.body: In the app installed on iPadOS 26 the blur came back over the bar when My settings or System opened, and after signing in, and stayed until the app was started again. The settings and the system had a bar of their own and sign-in had none. Now every page shares one bar that never leaves the screen. On the sign-in page it holds the language buttons; in a browser tab nothing changes.

small: The back arrow of My settings and System goes straight to your home board.
Thanks to bluedsticker for the report and the screenshots (#40).

0.41.2.lead: The bar keeps its order on an iPad held upright, however many pages a board has.

sections.title: Many pages, a narrow screen
sections.body: With many pages the search field ran under the bell and a long board name broke onto two lines. Narrow, the search field is now a plain search button, and the board name stays on one line. When the pages no longer fit, the row fades at the side where there are more, with an arrow there to turn it on, and the page you are on is always in sight.

small: Thanks to bluedsticker for the report and the screenshots (#40).

0.41.3.lead: Cards that start as a dial can show the plain number.

sections.title: The number instead of the dial
sections.body: NextDNS, Technitium, Pi-hole, AdGuard Home, Immich storage, Nextcloud storage and PeaNUT draw a dial by default, and their View list had no plain number. Choose The number there, and the value is drawn large with the other values under it. Cards already on a board stay as they are.

small: Thanks to naamah75 for the report (#44).

0.41.4.lead: The nexpaper deadlines card names a contract's last day to cancel.

sections.title: Last day to cancel
sections.body: nexpaper 1.4.0 and later also sends the last day to cancel a contract with a notice period, its end minus the notice. The Deadlines card showed it as the raw word notice and now names it Last day to cancel.

small: A board dragged to a new place in the board list no longer jumps back for a moment on a slow server.
Older nexpaper versions never send this day, so their cards stay as they were.
Apprise, which sends the notifications, is now 1.13.1: older versions passed a channel's login headers on when a service redirected to another host.

0.42.0.lead: The search under Ctrl K finds the links on the board.

sections.title: Links in the search
sections.body: The entries of a Bookmarks card, buttons that open an address and the saved links a Karakeep, Linkwarden or Linkding card shows now appear in the search as Link. Type a title or part of the address and press Enter to open it. The search asks no service for more than its card already shows.
sections.path: Ctrl K or the search field in the bar

small: Only the cards of the page that is open are searched, as before.
Thanks to luiscarrasco2324 for the idea (#46).

0.43.0.lead: A page that draws your UniFi network with the traffic on every link, liquid glass, and a colour for every card.

sections.title: The network plan
sections.body: A new kind of page shows your gateway, switches and access points as a tree, each on the port it hangs from, with the traffic of every link running in both directions and its load as colour. Add servers, NAS and other wired devices from a list; anything new waits under Found until you place it. Drag cards where you want them, and choose lines, dots or dashes in the display menu. UniFi only for now.

sections.title: Liquid glass
sections.body: A fifth card style: thick glass with a rim that catches the light and a glare that follows the pointer. A board can have a style of its own, and three bright backgrounds, Prism, Lagoon and Sunset, show the glass at its best.
sections.path: Settings > Appearance, or Board settings > Look

sections.title: A colour for every card
sections.body: Give a card one of eight colours, the main colour of its logo or a colour of your own, as a frame, a tint or the whole card. A card that is down keeps its red frame.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > a card's settings > Colour

sections.title: Big app tiles and container logos
sections.body: An app tile can show its name over a large logo, with reachability as a dot or as bars. Container lists show the logo of each container, from its image or a nexdeck.icon label.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > an app tile's settings > Display

small: Cards tip towards the mouse pointer; switch it off under Settings > Profile.
Two pages of one name each have an address of their own again.
Container log lines in the board stream only reach whoever may read that log.
The second sign-in step and the forgotten password have limits of their own.

0.44.0.lead: Pulse on the board: what it watches on Proxmox and Docker, and what needs a look.

sections.title: Pulse
sections.body: Three cards. The overview counts the active alerts and what Pulse watches: nodes, VMs, LXC and Docker containers, and how many resources are critical or need attention. Needs a look lists the resources Pulse is not happy with, worst first, with the reason, such as offline, a critical alert or an old backup. Active alerts shows critical alerts first and how long each has been open. A token with the preset Kiosk / Monitoring is enough; the cards only read.

small: Pulse starts as beta. Needs a look needs Pulse 6.5 or newer, the other cards 6.0.
Thanks to C0NN0RAD0 for the idea (#47).

0.45.0.lead: A page for your home, as a beta: lamps, heating, covers, scenes, switches, sensors and statistics from Home Assistant, placed freely.

sections.title: A page for your home
sections.body: A new kind of page holds the controls of Home Assistant on a free surface instead of the card grid, so a light switch takes the room of a light switch. Put headings over your rooms, place everything where you like it and grow or shrink a drawing by its corner. Every element can carry a name of your own. The lists to pick from leave out settings, diagnostics and anything hidden in Home Assistant.

sections.title: Lamps and thermostats
sections.body: Ten styles each, from a pill to a bulb, a dial or a radiator, mixed on one page. A tap switches a lamp, a drag sideways dims it, holding it opens brightness, white and colour. Swipe a thermostat to set the target or turn its dial; a tap opens mode, presets and its recent history.

sections.title: Covers, scenes and switches
sections.body: Covers as a window, slats, slider or pill, with open, close, stop and a position, or several on one card with positions of your own such as Morning. Scenes and scripts as pills, tiles, a bar or a grid. Switches and plugs as an outlet, rocker or toggle, with what the device draws; a switch can ask before it turns off.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > Cover, Scene or Switch

sections.title: Sensors and statistics
sections.body: Doors and windows, drawn or on one card, temperature and humidity per room, and hints such as a window open where the heating runs. Statistics cards draw Home Assistant's long-term statistics over 24 hours, 7 or 30 days, with now, low, high and mean.

small: Home pages follow the card style under Appearance, liquid glass and tilt included.
On a phone each heading keeps its elements under it, and a wall display switches them when its link allows actions.
A home page only ever calls the services of its own controls, and only for what stands on it. The lists need a token of a Home Assistant administrator.
Proxmox cards say which right the token is missing instead of staying empty (#48).

0.46.0.lead: TrueNAS shows much more: interfaces, apps, disks, backups, services and VMs, each as a card of its own.

sections.title: Network and apps
sections.body: Interfaces shows every network interface with its link, address, speed and live traffic, and draws download and upload over time. Apps lists every app with its state and version: crashed ones first, then those with a newer version or newer images waiting, each linked to its web page.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > Add widget > TrueNAS > Interfaces or Apps

sections.title: Disks
sections.body: Every disk with its temperature, model, pool and size. It turns yellow and red from 50 and 60 °C for spinning disks and from 70 and 80 °C for flash, or earlier where the disk names a lower limit of its own. Read at most every five minutes, because every reading reaches the disk; on TrueNAS 25.04 a sleeping disk is left asleep.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > Add widget > TrueNAS > Disks

sections.title: Data protection
sections.body: Snapshot, replication, cloud sync, rsync and cloud backup tasks with their last run. Failed ones come first and say why. Each kind can be switched off in the card's settings, and then it is not read at all.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > Add widget > TrueNAS > Data protection

sections.title: Services, VMs and containers
sections.body: Services shows SMB, NFS, SSH and the other services set to start with TrueNAS, red when one of them is stopped. VMs and containers lists virtual machines and Incus containers with their state, CPUs and memory.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > Add widget > TrueNAS > Services or VMs and containers

small: The System card shows a waiting TrueNAS update or a pending reboot, checked every six hours.
The Pools card shows the last scrub of each pool and turns yellow when it found errors.
Three new kinds of notification: a disk running hot, a failed backup task and an update waiting on a server.
The new cards are a beta and need TrueNAS 25.04 or later over https. A key with the Read-Only Administrator role is enough.
DOMPurify 3.4.17, which cleans what note cards show.
Thanks to AlexT59 for the idea and the digging into the API (#49).

0.47.0.lead: Your own name and logo, the versions of your services, groups you drag cards into, and a side bar that stays in place.

sections.title: Name and logo
sections.body: Give the installation a name and a logo of your own. They stand where nexdeck's do: in the browser tab, in the bar, on the sign-in page, under the icon of the installed app and on wall displays. The board's name can stand in front in the tab. The sign-in page shows both, so anyone who reaches the address sees them.

sections.title: Versions of your services
sections.body: The Updates card lists every connected service whose version is behind the newest release of its project on GitHub, with the newer version linked to its release notes. Under System, Integrations each connection shows the version it runs. GitHub is only asked while Check for updates is on, which it is not by default.
sections.path: System > About > Check for updates, then Edit mode (pencil) > Updates card > Connected services

sections.title: Groups you drag cards into
sections.body: While arranging, drag a card onto a group to put it inside, and drag it out again onto the board. Inside, every card gets a width and a height of its own from the two buttons at its foot, so a wide card can stand beside two small ones. The group grows with what it holds.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > drag a card onto a group

sections.title: A side bar per page
sections.body: Left or right of the board, narrow or wide. Drag cards into it like into a group and give each its height. It stays where it is while the page scrolls, stands above the board on a phone and shows on wall displays.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > Side bar above the board

small: A kiosk link shows a network plan instead of an empty page.
The Add page dialog lists the kinds of page one under the other, readable at last.
A network plan is loaded when its page opens: the first load of every board is lighter.

0.48.0.lead: Numbers from several services in one grid for the wall, a countdown and a kitchen timer, Uptime Kuma by status page, and pages you put in your own order.

sections.title: Key figures
sections.body: A new card that shows numbers from several services side by side, such as the processor of the NAS, the downloads and the blocked queries. Each tile is a number card of the page and keeps its own settings, its yellow and red lines included. The grid works out its rows by itself, or keeps to the columns you choose, and the numbers grow with the card.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > Add widget > Key figures, then drag number cards onto it

sections.title: Countdown and timer
sections.body: The countdown shows the days until a date, and hours and minutes once it is close; every year for a birthday. The timer starts, pauses and resets, with quick picks that start at once. When it is done the card flashes until somebody taps it and rings for a minute. Each browser runs its own timer.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > Add widget > Countdown or Timer

sections.title: Uptime Kuma by status page
sections.body: The Monitors card and the Up and down card can keep to the monitors of one status page; type its slug, the last part of its address. The summary names the monitors that are down. Uptime Kuma is no longer a beta.
sections.path: Uptime Kuma card > Settings > Status page

sections.title: Pages in your order
sections.body: Every page has a handle in the board settings. Drag it, or press the arrow keys on it, and the tabs follow.

small: Uptime Kuma no longer shows "-1 ms" for groups and push monitors, and no longer counts a monitor called "?".
With a name filter, the Uptime Kuma card counts and colours only the monitors it shows.
undici 7.30.1 and serialize-javascript 7.1.4 in the test and build tools.
Thanks to mplok1 for asking for the order of pages (#50).

0.49.0.lead: nexdeck starts to understand your homelab: a card that says what needs a look, a chronicle of what changed and since when, a chat you can ask, history over months, what runs on what, and a page that says why something broke.

sections.title: Needs attention
sections.body: The Problems card grew into a card that says what needs a look, from every board: cards that are yellow or red with their reason and since when, services whose check fails, and the warnings of the bell you have not read. A row leads to the card. What does not fit becomes "Show 16 more". Cards you already have keep doing what they did.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > Add widget > Needs attention

sections.title: Maintenance
sections.body: Put a connection or an app tile into maintenance for a few hours or until a time. Until then nothing about it is told, no outage is opened, and the availability bars draw the time grey. The card says until when. Administrators only.

sections.title: Chronicle and daily report
sections.body: One page with what changed, newest first: cards that turned yellow, red or green, outages, new versions, containers that restarted, and changes made in nexdeck. A yellow or red card now says since when. The cards What happened and Daily report show it on a board, and the daily report can arrive as a message every morning. Backrest, Kopia and Duplicati turn yellow when the last good backup is too old.
sections.path: Account menu > Chronicle; Settings > Notifications > Daily report

sections.title: Ask nexdeck
sections.body: A chat for administrators next to the bell. It answers from your cards, the chronicle and the history, and shows where it looked. It never presses a button: it shows the button with what it would hit, such as the streams that end when Plex restarts, and you press it. It reads a container's log only after you allow it. Off until you choose Claude or a model on your own network, such as Ollama.
sections.path: System > Assistant, then the sparkle next to the bell

sections.title: History over months and forecasts
sections.body: nexdeck keeps hour averages for 90 days and day averages for two years of every number. A chart card has buttons for 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days and a year, with the lowest to the highest as a band. A quiet line at the foot of a card says when a volume is full or a number reaches its red line, and under 14 days you get a message.
sections.path: The buttons on a chart card

sections.title: What runs on what
sections.body: nexdeck asks Docker, Portainer, a Synology and Proxmox which containers and guests they run, and works out which service runs in which, through Nginx Proxy Manager too. What it only guesses waits for your yes. When a host goes down, you get one message that names what it took with it, and their cards say why.

sections.title: Why is it broken?
sections.body: A red or yellow card has a "Why?" that opens a page of its service: since when, what happened in the two hours before, what it runs on, its check and cards, the log of its container when you ask for it, and a runbook you write once for next time. "Explain it" hands the page to the chat.
sections.path: "Why?" on a red or yellow card

small: The question before a button says what it would hit: streams that end, downloads that stop, the lights a scene switches, what runs in a container or a guest.
The Updates card takes Arcane and Dockhand as container sources. Thanks to mplok1 for the idea (#51).
A page the browser translated no longer goes blank when something on it changes.
The Updates card says how old a newer release is.

0.50.0.lead: nexdeck gets a look of its own: 1984, where every card is a window. Light and dark follow the system or the clock, cards can be copied and hidden, the weather and the calendar say more, the integrations have a page of their own, and 22 services join.

sections.body: The whole of nexdeck drawn as an early desktop: every card a window with a striped title bar, the bar a menu bar, the page a dotted desk, titles in pixel type, black on white and inverted for the night. A yellow card is hatched and a red one turns black, so a status never rests on colour alone. Choose a touch of colour or the pattern only, black and white logos, and the desk.

sections.title: Light, dark and type
sections.body: Light and dark follow the system the moment it switches, or the clock: two times of day, for each account and for each wall display link. Besides the glass there is a calm card style, six types for the interface (Inter, the system's own, IBM Plex Sans, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, Geist, JetBrains Mono) and an editor for a colour theme of your own.

sections.title: Copy, hide, swipe, keys
sections.body: Copy a card onto the same page or onto a page of another board, a group with the cards it holds. Hide a card on the phone, unless it turns red. Swipe between pages on a phone and on a wall display. Press 1 to 9 to open an app tile, and ? shows which key is which.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > the move menu of a card, Copy to

sections.title: Weather and calendar
sections.body: The weather card can show the next 12 or 24 hours with the chance of rain, the air quality, the UV index and pollen. The calendar card shows a week or a month as a grid, each source in its own colour, and the arrows page for you alone.
sections.path: Edit mode (pencil) > Weather or Calendar card > Settings

sections.title: A page for your integrations
sections.body: The counts at the top are filters: failing, updates, without a card, muted. Failing connections come first, there is a list by category, and the catalog behind Add an integration is a window with a search. At its top, Found in your network lists the services your containers and guests run that you have not connected yet, with the address filled in.

sections.title: Short names and a search engine
sections.body: Every app tile has a short name, and /go/<name> opens it. Add nexdeck as a search engine in Chrome, Edge or Firefox, and a short name typed in the address bar opens its tile, other words open the search, with suggestions as you type. Safari cannot do this.

sections.title: 22 new integrations
sections.body: aria2, pyLoad, Jackett, Ombi, slskd, Kodi, Owncast, PeerTube, rclone, Stash, xTeVe, Your Spotify, Spoolman, Moonraker, openHAB, Homebridge, Node-RED, ESPHome, Tasmota, Shelly, OpenDTU and Fronius, with buttons where the service has something safe to press. All of them start as beta.

sections.title: Tighter by default
sections.body: API tokens can be read only, and new ones are: they look but never change anything. The picture relay sends a service only the picture paths its integration names, where any path could reach it with the credentials of the connection, such as marking a title as watched in Plex. A redirect to another place takes no credentials along.

small: A card can go without its head and without its frame, for a clock or a line of text that should stand free.
A card or connection without a logo shows the one its service names for itself.
FRITZ!Box takes an optional user and is out of beta; behind a bridge it no longer turns red with an uptime of 0 seconds.
Menus on home pages stay in view, and the text on the accent colour reads on a light accent too.

0.51.0.lead: 39 services join, and the card style you chose now reaches the whole of nexdeck. 1984 draws the network plan in bold lines, and the accent reads on the light theme.

sections.title: 39 new integrations
sections.body: Zerobyte (backup schedules with a Run now button, yellow when the last good backup is too old), a UPS read from NUT itself, Caddy, Garage, Keycloak, Stalwart 1.0, SFTPGo, Jenkins, Woodpecker CI, a container registry, Synapse, BookStack, Wiki.js, Trilium, Memos, Readeck, KitchenOwl, LubeLogger, Planka, Traccar and many more, and three new GitHub cards: a repository, pull requests with their checks, and milestones. All of them start as beta.

sections.title: The card style follows you everywhere
sections.body: Flat, Outline, Calm, Neon edge and Liquid glass are now drawn on the boxes of the settings and System, on sheets, dialogs, menus, the search behind Ctrl K and the assistant too, not only on the cards. A board with a style of its own changes its own cards only.

sections.title: Light theme: an accent you can read
sections.body: On the light page the accent is darkened in its own hue until it reads as text, cyan becomes a deeper teal, and the same goes for colours of your own. The dark theme keeps what it had.

sections.title: 1984: the network plan
sections.body: The links of the topology plan are solid black lines with a border of paper, thicker the busier the link is, dashed when it is down, on a calm grey instead of the dots of the desk.

small: /go/<name> and Ctrl K now find an app tile that opens the address of its connection, instead of falling back to the search.
The saved bookmarks of a Readeck card can be found in Ctrl K.
A UPS read through NUT sends a message when it runs on battery and when the mains are back.
30 more services say when their project has a newer release.

Security: the kept answers of a service are no longer shared between two sign-ins, and an error answer is not kept. The dependency audit lets one build-tool advisory pass until the end of the year, with its reason.

0.52.0.lead: Claude Code, claude.ai and other MCP programs can now read your boards and press a card's button once you allow it. A hanging service costs less, and the bell counts on every page.

sections.title: AI from outside (MCP)
sections.body: A program such as Claude Code or claude.ai reads what needs a look, your cards, the chronicle and the history of a number, with the rights of your account and only the boards you give it. Each key has its level, its boards, an end and a right per tool: allow, ask me first or deny. A press that asks comes to the bell with Allow and Decline and runs out after ten minutes; a dangerous button always asks, and twice. Programs that sign in themselves connect over OAuth, with a consent page in nexdeck. Off until an administrator switches it on.
sections.path: System > AI from outside (MCP); My settings > AI from outside (MCP)

sections.title: Calmer when a service hangs
sections.body: When several cards of one connection ask the same thing at the same time, nexdeck sends one request and hands the answer to all of them, also while a slow service is still thinking. A hanging service gets half the requests it got before, and the others keep their pace. A card no longer shows an answer older than it asked for.

sections.title: Wiki.js: recent comments
sections.body: A new card lists the newest comments with their page, who wrote them and how long ago, and each row opens the discussion. Wiki.js only hands out the comments of one page at a time, so on a large wiki the card reads the pages in rounds and says so until it has read them all.

small: The bell counts new notices on every page, not only on a board, and after a reload it shows the right number at once.
Calendar cards put an episode on the day of your own clock, not the day in UTC, so an evening show no longer lands on the next day.
The Speedtest Tracker history shows the latest measurements on a tracker with more than one page of results.
After an update, a service shows as current within the hour instead of six.
The inventory no longer proposes a device such as a FRITZ!Box in a container that only shares part of its name.
The chronicle no longer lists the card lines of a board you may not open when two boards share a connection.
The foot of the bell wraps on a narrow drawer and a phone instead of breaking its labels.

1.0.0.lead: nexdeck 1.0: build cards of your own out of any service, without code, and share them in the Card shop, or take one somebody else made.

sections.title: Custom cards
sections.body: Pick a connection, ask it once and click the values you want in its answer. The card shows them as a number, a few numbers, a list, a wall of pictures or a free layout of twelve blocks, with buttons if you like. The editor shows a live preview, and a YAML view shows the same card for the special cases. Only administrators build cards; users see them on the boards shared with them.

sections.title: Integrations of your own
sections.body: For an app nexdeck does not know, describe the address, the form and how it signs in: a key, a user and password or a session. Cards then read it like any other connection, and it can show whether the service is up and its version.

sections.title: The Card shop
sections.body: Switch it on to browse the cards others shared, see one with your own data before you take it, install it and get its updates. Share your own straight from nexdeck with your GitHub name, or start a new card from one of the examples.

small: With an AI set up, the editor drafts a card from one sentence, changes it and translates its texts, and Ask nexdeck makes a draft from the chat.
Custom cards and integrations go out as a file, and a board export takes the custom cards on it along.
A custom card only reads, asks only the address of its connection and never gets its keys.

1.0.1.lead: The card help now builds cards that work: it reads your service before it shows you a proposal.

sections.title: Ask AI checks its own card
sections.body: The AI is shown the paths nexdeck already reads from the service, and nexdeck asks every path of its proposal before you see it. A path the service does not know, or fields the answer does not have, go back to the AI once, so the card reads what your service really sends. The preview beside the proposal now shows the card with example data made from that answer.
sections.path: System > Custom cards > Build a card > Ask AI

small: Years show as 2005, not 2,005, on every custom card.
The step Data offers only paths a card can read; paths that need a window of dates are gone.
The hint under a failure of a custom card is in your language, and the selection in the YAML editors is readable in the dark.
